articles.title_zh: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
facts_zh:
Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
- Published
A bodycam video has been released by Ukraine police which they say shows the moments between two powerful Russian bomb strikes that killed at least 40 people at an aid centre and a shelter.
The footage, from a camera on one of the killed police officers, shows residents of the southern village of Kamyshuvakha going to an underground shelter after the first attack on Monday.
Soon after a blast is heard and flames are seen as the shelter is hit.

articles.title_zh: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
facts_zh:
US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
- Published
It was the midterm result that many in Canada had hoped for - a Democratic sweep that was in part a repudiation by American voters of Donald Trump's tariff on close trade allies.
"I was doing cartwheels down the street," said Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Wednesday morning, calling it "a victory for Canada".

Tuesday night's result is unlikely to grant Canada relief from those tariffs any time soon, but there is anticipation that the political shifts could create a more favourable environment for Ottawa to get the best deal now that on-again-off-again trade talks are back on.

Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock
- Published
Israel's President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with political parties on whom to task with forming a new coalition government, after he received the official results of a general election last week he said had no clear winner.
Herzog told party leaders that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid a new election.
Neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament.

articles.title_original: Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism
articles.title_zh: Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism
facts_zh:
Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism
- Published
Hungary has opened communist-era secret police files to the public, in a controversial move the government says will help Hungarian society heal itself from the traumas of 45 years of communist rule.
Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and that the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish to family members.
The date of the opening is symbolic - on 4 November 1956 Soviet tanks rolled through Budapest and other cities, to crush Hungary's short-lived revolution.

all_titles.en: Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism

articles.title_zh: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force
facts_zh:
Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force
- Published
Delhi is once again battling worsening air pollution as the onset of winter brings a familiar deterioration in air quality to India's capital.

The city's air quality index (AQI) - which measures PM2.5, fine particulate matter that can clog lungs - has crossed 300, entering the "very poor" category and raising health concerns for millions of residents.
Breathing such polluted air over prolonged periods can cause respiratory problems and worsen existing illnesses, with children and older people particularly vulnerable.
